title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Setting (from p.82): take two totally ordered 'segments' I, I' that share a smallest element 0 and a largest element 1. The figure on p.82 draws them as two arcs from 0 to 1, the boundary of a disc. Let J^0 = I x I'. A point z = (x, x') is pictured as a chord joining x on the upper arc to x' on the lower arc. It is treated as a 1-dimensional stratum whose 'open stratum' A_z = {z} is declared open, being the complement of the closed 'half-lines' [z'',1] (z''>z) and [0,z'] (z'<z). The natural support function takes values in subsets of I ⊔ I' (glued at 0 and 1): |z| = {x, x'}, |0| = {0}, |1| = {1}. On p.82 Grothendieck shows that for incomparable z1 = (x1,x'1), z2 = (x2,x'2) (with x1 < x2 but x'2 < x'1, i.e. the chords do not cross), the support of an intersection B_{z1} ∩ B_{z2} is strictly smaller than the intersection of supports. This page gives the dual phenomenon and a non-distributivity counterexample. (1) For A = {z1, z2}, the set-theoretic support is |A| = |z1| ∪ |z2| = {x1, x2, x'1, x'2}. But sup A = A_{z1} ∨ A_{z2}, the join in the lattice of open 'supports', is the whole quadrilateral strip between the two chords. Its support on the boundary is [x1,x2] ∪ [x'2,x'1]. Hence |A| ⊊ |sup A|: the support map does not commute with sup. (2) Take a chord z3 = (x3, x'3) strictly between them (x1<x3<x2, x'2<x'3<x'1). Then A_{z3} ≤ A_{z1} ∨ A_{z2}, so A_{z3} ∧ (A_{z1} ∨ A_{z2}) = A_{z3}. But A_{z3} ∧ A_{z1} = A_{z3} ∧ A_{z2} = ∅, so (A_{z3}∧A_{z1}) ∨ (A_{z3}∧A_{z2}) = ∅. The lattice of open supports in this stratified 'space without points' is therefore not distributive, hence not a frame/locale. (3) Scholie: the formalism of supports is sound, provided one does not compare supports of strata with those of compatible figures, nor use it in contexts that require set-like (distributive) behaviour. The bracketed remark apparently cites notions such as dimension or quasi-set-theoretic constructions and earlier formal definitions. This motivates p.84: define intrinsic open strata X° = supp X ∩ cosupp ∂X and test whether supp X = Sup of the Y° for Y ≤ X. The page belongs to Grothendieck's attempt, in Analysis situs, to found a combinatorial/axiomatic tame topology of stratified 'éditions' and 'figures', where 'opens' form a lattice rather than a Boolean algebra of point sets.
errors: The text says 'propriété modulaire (ou distributivité de ∧ par rapport à ∨)'. The computation shows failure of distributivity only. Modularity is a weaker law, and failure of distributivity does not by itself refute modularity. To exhibit non-modularity one would need an N5 (pentagon) sublattice; the three atoms A_{z1}, A_{z2}, A_{z3} as given more naturally suggest M3- or N5-type behaviour, which is not checked. Minor conflation, though N5 may well be present.
The interval on the lower arc is written [x'1,x'2], but with x'2 < x'1 it should be [x'2,x'1], as on p.82.

The 'sup' operation (join of open supports) is not explicitly defined on this page; the claim that A_{z1} ∨ A_{z2} is the full strip relies on the implicit definition of the lattice of figures from earlier pages.

ideas.what: Support map from strata/figures to boundary point-sets does not commute with joins (|A| ⊊ |sup A|) nor meets (p.82)
ideas.modern_name: failure of a support map to be a lattice homomorphism; non-spatial lattice of 'opens'

ideas.what: Lattice of open supports of a stratified configuration (chords in a disc) is non-distributive
ideas.modern_name: non-distributive lattice of subobjects (non-frame), cf. lattices of convex sets / subspaces

ideas.what: Programmatic restriction ('scholie') on when the support formalism may be used, within an axiomatic tame topology of strata/figures
ideas.modern_name: tame topology / stratified spaces, Esquisse d'un programme §5
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programme); o-minimality by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches tame topology in general; this specific formalism is not published

missed.claim: The page documents that Grothendieck's pointless 'figure/support' axiomatics for tame topology yields non-distributive lattices of opens. Distributivity holds automatically in o-minimal (Boolean) settings. This is a design obstacle in his unpublished Analysis situs, not a result missed by the literature.
missed.quote: donc on n'a pas la propriété modulaire (ou distributivité de ∧ par ∨)!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for understanding why the 1986 Analysis situs approach differs from o-minimality; mathematically elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine counterexample showing a lattice is non-distributive and a support map is not a lattice morphism; interesting only as a step in Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: '[x'_1, x'_2]' in |sup A| is as written, but mathematically should be [x'_2, x'_1].
'z_3 = (x_3, x'_3) avec[?]': the image shows a dash-like connector ('...') before the inequalities x1<x3<x2, x'2<x'3<x'1.

Scholie reads approximately: 'Le formalisme des supports est bon, pourvu qu'on ne s'avise pas de comparer les supports des strates et des figures compatibles, ou s'en servir dans des contextes qui ne puissent ... (Tel est le cas des notions de dimension, ... quasi-ensemblistes, ... les définitions formelles ...)'. The last two lines are very cramped and largely illegible.
